testResults.name: workflow-static-syntax
testResults.result: actionlint 1.7.12, with ShellCheck 0.11.0 available, reported no diagnostics for the workflow YAML, GitHub Actions expressions, reusable-workflow call, job dependencies, permissions, and shell blocks

testResults.name: main-branch-and-concurrency-boundary
testResults.result: The workflow has a push-only master trigger with relevant path filters, a non-canceling deployment concurrency group, and an explicit deploy-job condition for refs/heads/master; it has no workflow_dispatch or alternate mutation trigger

testResults.name: reusable-image-publication
testResults.result: The publish-image job calls ./.github/workflows/publish-image.yml, grants packages: write only to that reusable job, and passes its image-reference and image-digest outputs to the deployment job

testResults.name: immutable-image-contract
testResults.result: The deployment fails unless the reusable-workflow outputs are a matching GHCR sha256 reference and digest, passes the digest reference to sharedImageReference, then verifies both the API container and ingest job use that exact reference

testResults.name: oidc-and-least-privilege
testResults.result: The deployment job uses azure/login with id-token: write and variable-backed client, tenant, and subscription identifiers; no Azure client secret, provider/API secret, subscription ID, resource group name, or email is embedded

testResults.name: manual-approval-and-single-mutation-path
testResults.result: The deployment job targets the repository-selected GitHub Environment before any Azure login or mutation; required reviewers on that Environment are the manual approval gate, and the workflow comments and trigger boundary identify this as the only repository-managed production mutation path

testResults.name: probe-safe-health-smoke
testResults.result: After deployment, the workflow derives the deployed API FQDN, calls the source-defined unauthenticated /health endpoint with curl retries, and requires JSON status=ok without handling a bearer, provider, or API credential
